about: Everything factory/dog_roll.py can draw for a generated dog still. The aim is a dog that passes for someone's own pet, photographed by its owner on a phone, with no two stills alike (floor real-scruffy-dogs, Krish, 10 Nov: "way too perfect and not real"). The roller draws every attribute from here; a session never chooses or rewrites one. Each light is data: what it looks like, the colour cast it gives the phone, and whether a bulb or lamp is itself bright in the frame. Nothing here may name a product (mug, blanket, portrait, card), a human expression, words in the frame, a person, or a chestnut or red dachshund.

cast_lines.warm: the phone's white balance leaning orange under the warm light, giving the fur a golden tint
cast_lines.cool: a white balance on the blue side, so the darker fur reads a little blue-gray
cast_lines.neutral: close to neutral white balance, only a touch warm on the coat
cast_lines.fluorescent: a faint green tint from the tube light, strongest in the darker areas
cast_lines.mixed: two colors of light the phone never quite settles between: one half of the frame warm, the other cool

bright_source: the bulb itself burned out to a flat white spot
a small, faint flare from the bulb near the top edge of the frame
daylight: any window or patch of sky burned out to plain white
highlights.flicker: thin bands of flicker running across the frame from the ceiling tubes

artifacts: shadows pulled up by the phone's HDR, so the contrast looks a bit flat
over-sharpened fur and whiskers with slightly crunchy edges
the darkest patches of fur smudged soft by noise reduction, almost painterly
{compression} compression showing faint blocks in plain areas such as the wall and floor
a thin purple fringe on bright edges
exposure set on the dog, so the brightest parts run hot and the corners go a little dark
the horizon a degree or two off level
focus landing just behind the dog, so it is a hair soft
a small blur on the tail or one paw where it moved
a small, flat reflection of the room light in the eyes, never a studio catchlight
